# Approximations for Distributions

```{r initialise}
set.seed(16122020)
library(ggplot2)
n.simulations <- 1e6
```      

## Hypergeometric and Binomial

```{r hyp-binom, fig.height=5,warning=FALSE}
hyper_binom_histogram <- function(n,N,M){
  data1 <- data.frame(x=rhyper(n.simulations,M,N-M,n),name="Hypergeometric")
  data2 <- data.frame(x=rbinom(n.simulations,n,M/N),name="Binomial")
  ggplot(data=rbind(data1,data2)) + aes(x=x,group=name,colour=name) + 
    geom_histogram(binwidth=1,center=0,fill="white",position="identity",linewidth=0.1) + 
    geom_freqpoly(aes(linetype=name),binwidth=1,center=0,position="identity") + 
    ggtitle(paste0("Hypergeometric vs Binomial with ",n,
                   " trials in population of size ",N," having ",M," successes")) + 
    theme(legend.title=element_blank(),legend.justification=c(1,1),
          legend.position=c(0.9,0.9),plot.margin=unit(c(0,0,1,0),"cm")) + 
    xlab("Number of successes") + xlim(-1,n+1)
}
for(N in c(10,20,50,100,200)){
  print(hyper_binom_histogram(10,N,0.5*N))
}
```    

## Poisson and Binomial

```{r pois-binom, fig.height=5,warning=FALSE}
poisson_binom_histogram <- function(lambda,n){
  data1 <- data.frame(x=rpois(n.simulations,lambda),name="Poisson")
  data2 <- data.frame(x=rbinom(n.simulations,n,lambda/n),name="Binomial")
  ggplot(data=rbind(data1,data2)) + aes(x=x,group=name,colour=name) + 
    geom_histogram(binwidth=1,center=0,fill="white",position="identity",linewidth=0.1) + 
    geom_freqpoly(aes(linetype=name),binwidth=1,center=0,position="identity") + 
    ggtitle(paste0("Poisson with ",lambda," expected successes vs Binomial with ",n,
                   " trials and probability of success ",lambda/n)) + 
    theme(legend.title=element_blank(),legend.justification=c(1,1), 
          legend.position=c(0.9,0.9),plot.margin=unit(c(0,0,1,0),"cm")) + 
    xlab("Number of successes") + xlim(-1,n+5)
}
for(n in c(10,20,50,100,200)){
  print(poisson_binom_histogram(10,n))
}
```    

## Binomial and Normal

```{r binom-norm, fig.height=5,warning=FALSE}
cols <- c("FIRST"="red","SECOND"="black")
binom_normal_histogram <- function(n,p){
  data <- data.frame(x=rbinom(n.simulations,n,p))
  ggplot(data) + aes(x=x) + 
    geom_histogram(binwidth=1,center=0,fill="white",colour="blue",
                   linetype="dashed",linewidth=0.1) + 
    geom_freqpoly(binwidth=1,center=0,aes(colour="FIRST"),linetype="dotted",linewidth=1) + 
    stat_function(fun=function(x) n.simulations*dnorm(x,mean=n*p,sd=sqrt(n*p*(1-p))),
                  aes(color="SECOND"),linetype="solid",linewidth=0.5) + 
    ggtitle(paste0("Binomial Distribution with ",n,
                   " trials and probability of success ",p)) + 
    scale_colour_manual(values=cols,labels=c("Binomial","Normal")) + 
    theme(legend.title=element_blank(),legend.justification=c(1,1), 
          legend.position=c(0.9,0.9),plot.margin=unit(c(0,0,1,0),"cm")) + 
    xlab("Number of successes") + xlim(-1,n+1)
}
for(n in c(5,10,20,50,100,200)){
  print(binom_normal_histogram(n,0.5))
}
```    

Remark: The DataCamp course (for example, see  https://campus.datacamp.com/courses/foundations-of-probability-in-r/related-distributions?ex=3) uses the following code to compare two distributions:
```{r datacamp-compare}
compare_histograms <- function(variable1, variable2) {
  x <- data.frame(value = variable1, variable = "Variable 1")
  y <- data.frame(value = variable2, variable = "Variable 2")
  ggplot(rbind(x, y), aes(value)) +
    geom_histogram() +
    facet_wrap(~ variable, nrow = 2)
}
```     

## Normal Distribution

### Exponential and Linear function
The following plot illustrates the difference in bounds given by the law of large numbers 
and by the normal distribution tails.
```{r lin-exp,fig.height=5}
curve(exp,0,3,col="red",lty=1,xlim=c(0,20),ylab="",asp=1,las=1)
text(log(15),15,"y=e^x",col="red",pos=4,cex=2)
curve(x^1,col="black",lty=2,add=TRUE)
text(15,15,"y=x",pos=4,cex=2,offset=1)
```     

### The Central Limit Theorem

Let's consider the distribution of the sample mean 
for different sample sizes and different distributions of the original random variable.
The red line shows the density of the respective normal approximation.

```{r show-distr-setup}
show.mean.distribution <- function(n,smpl.gen,orig=FALSE,n.bins=200,h.center=0){
  random.sample <- smpl.gen(n,n.simulations)
  if (is.function(n.bins))
    n.bins <- n.bins(random.sample) 
  if(orig){
    print(
      ggplot(data.frame(x=random.sample)) + aes(x=x) + 
        geom_histogram(aes(y=stat(density)),bins=n.bins,center=h.center,
                       fill="black",colour="white",linewidth=0.1) + 
        ggtitle("Distribution of the Original Random Variable")
    )  
  }
  distr.mean <- mean(random.sample)
  distr.sd <- sd(random.sample)
  means <- apply(matrix(random.sample,ncol=n),1,mean)
  print(
    ggplot(data.frame(x=means)) + aes(x=x) +
      geom_histogram(aes(y=stat(density)),bins=n.bins,center=h.center,
                     fill="black",colour="white",linewidth=0.1) +
      stat_function(fun=function(x)dnorm(x,mean=distr.mean,sd=distr.sd/sqrt(n)),
                    color="red",linetype="solid",linewidth=0.5) + 
      ggtitle(paste0("Distribution of the Sample Mean, sample size is ",n)) 
  )
}
```    

A uniform distribution:
```{r conv-unif, fig.align='center', fig.width=10}
unif.sample <- function(n,reps){
  runif(n*reps)
}
show.mean.distribution(2,unif.sample,TRUE)
for(n in c(5,15,30)){
  show.mean.distribution(n,unif.sample)
}
```    


An exponential distribution:
```{r conv-exp, fig.align='center', fig.width=10}
exp.sample <- function(n,reps){
  rexp(n*reps)
}
show.mean.distribution(2,exp.sample,TRUE)
for(n in c(5,15,30,50,100,200)){
  show.mean.distribution(n,exp.sample)
}
```    


A mixture of two uniform distributions:
```{r conv-2unif, fig.align='center', fig.width=10}
unifm.sample <- function(n,reps){
  runif(n*reps) + sample(c(0,2),n*n.simulations,replace=TRUE)
}
show.mean.distribution(2,unifm.sample,TRUE)
for(n in c(5,15,30)){
  show.mean.distribution(n,unifm.sample)
}
```    


A mixture of ten uniform distributions:
```{r conv-10unif, fig.align='center', fig.width=10}
unifm10.sample <- function(n,reps){
  runif(n*reps) + sample(2*(0:10),n*n.simulations,replace=TRUE)
}
show.mean.distribution(2,unifm10.sample,TRUE)
for(n in c(5,15,30)){
  show.mean.distribution(n,unifm10.sample)
}
```    


A binomial distribution:
```{r conv-binom, fig.align='center', fig.width=10}
binom.size <- 30
binom.sample <- function(n,reps){
  rbinom(n*reps,size=binom.size,prob=0.1)
}
```     

A wrong visualisation:
```{r conv-binom-wrong-visual, fig.align='center', fig.width=10}
show.mean.distribution(2,binom.sample,TRUE)
for(n in c(5,15,30,50,100)){
  show.mean.distribution(n,binom.sample)
}
```     

A better visualisation:
```{r conv-binom-right-visual, fig.align='center', fig.width=10}
show.mean.distribution(2,binom.sample,TRUE,n.bins=function(smpl){max(smpl)+1},h.center=pi/10)
for(n in c(5,15,30,50,100,200)){
  show.mean.distribution(n,binom.sample,n.bins=function(smpl){max(smpl)+round(n^(2/3))},h.center=pi/10)
}
```
